record.paper_title: Polycyclic Codes Associated with Trinomials: Good Codes and Open Questions
record.original_question: Is a polycyclic code over a finite field F_q self-dual exactly in the following situation: its generator polynomial has the form g(x) = x^m - a, it divides a trinomial x^(2m) - b x^m - c, and the scalar a satisfies a^2 = q - 1? In addition, if such a self-dual polycyclic code exists, must its minimum distance always be 2, and must every self-dual polycyclic code of this kind in fact be constacyclic rather than genuinely more general polycyclic?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.7. A polycyclic code over Fq is self-dual if and only if its generator is in the form g = x^m - a|x^(2m) - bx^m - c, where a^2 = q - 1. Also, the minimum distance of all self-dual polycyclic codes is 2 and they are all actually constacyclic codes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q$ elements. For a monic polynomial $f(x)\in\mathbb{F}_q[x]$ of degree $n$, a polycyclic code associated with $f$ is an ideal of the quotient ring $\mathbb{F}_q[x]/\langle f(x)\rangle$; equivalently, it is a linear subspace $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ that is closed under the linear shift induced by multiplication by $x$ modulo $f(x)$. Such a code $C$ is generated, as an ideal, by a monic divisor $g(x)$ of $f(x)$, called the generator polynomial of $C$. The code $C$ is called constacyclic if it is polycyclic with respect to a binomial $f(x)=x^n-\lambda$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_q^*$. The dual code $C^\perp$ is defined with respect to the standard Euclidean inner product on $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, and $C$ is self-dual if $C=C^\perp$.

Determine whether the following statement is true: a polycyclic code $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is self-dual if and only if there exist a positive integer $m$, elements $a,b,c\in\mathbb{F}_q$, and a trinomial $f(x)=x^{2m}-bx^m-c$ such that $C$ is the polycyclic code associated with $f$ having generator polynomial $g(x)=x^m-a$, with $g(x)\mid f(x)$ and $a^2=-1$ in $\mathbb{F}_q$. Moreover, decide whether every such self-dual polycyclic code necessarily has minimum Hamming distance equal to $2$ and is in fact a constacyclic code (rather than a strictly more general polycyclic code).
artifact.status_search_result: A follow-up work "On the duality and the direction of polycyclic codes" by Alahmadi et al. discusses duality and corrections to results on polycyclic codes, but the search did not produce conclusive evidence that this specific conjecture (characterizing self-dual polycyclic codes via the divisor $x^m-a$ of a trinomial with $a^2=-1$, minimum distance 2, and constacyclicity) has been proven or disproven. Status remains unverified from available sources.
